article.body:
chayolim just like you. Welcome to our podcast, where

Chayolim, in what way can this week’s lesson make a difference to you? What changes can you make in your own life?

But … don’t let it stop here! Conduct your own interviews at the Shabbos table. Choose someone

to be the podcast’s guest, and together explore how to live with the messages from the parsha.

Can we call the gardener today? I want to start my own garden one day.

Good afternoon, children! I was just checking on my red strings, but I can take a break to chat.

Oh, Yossi, silly! You know that strings don’t grow on trees.

Haha, Basya, of course I know. I was just joking. But Mr. Gardener, what are red strings doing in your garden and why do you need to check on them?

Ah, I put these strings there myself. You see, earlier this season, I spotted my first ripe pomegranate over here. So, I tied a red string around it. I’ve done the same with the other shiv’as haminim, to keep track of which fruits I will use for the special mitzvah of bikkurim.

Oh, we learned about this! Bikkurim are the first fruits that you bring to the Beis Hamikdash for Hashem!

Exactly! I’m picking out the most beautiful fruits that have grown. I will give Hashem the most perfect and delicious ones! As it says in this week's parsha, ”.רֵאשִׁית ּבִּכּורֵי אַדְמָתְָך ּתָבִיא ּבֵית ה' אֱֹלקֶיָך“ Well, really, I’ll bring it to the Beis Hamikdash, and give it to the kohen. This way, I'll have given my bikkurim to Hashem.

One day, I’m going to have a garden in Eretz Yisroel, and I’m going to bring the first and best fruits to Hashem, too! I wish I could start now, though. Even here, and even in Golus.

You definitely can! I think you actually already do, every day. You give the first and best of yourself to Hashem in the morning, when you are all rested and full of energy.

You mean when we jump up and say Modeh Ani? Is Modeh Ani our way of giving bikkurim to Hashem?

That’s the first thing I do every morning. I say it loud and clear! Even ask Mimi!

Yup, she’s on the bottom of our bunk bed. Every morning, Basya’s like my alarm clock—she always wakes me up when she says Modeh Ani. She jumps up like a lion!

So, if Modeh Ani is our way of giving bikkurim, then I’m sure Hashem loves Basya’s bikkurim!

I hope so. It’s one of my favorite mitzvos! I say Modeh Ani and then continue to thank Hashem for all the other good stuff He gives us. Like the Torah!

Right. We also show Hashem how grateful we are for the Torah by learning happily and doing mitzvos.

Amazing. And remember what Hashem told us earlier in Parshas Ki Sisa, right before this mitzvah?

Oh, I just learned this in Chumash class! It’s about Pesach, right? In this parsha, Hashem says to be very careful about staying away from chametz.

Chametz! Yes, the food that rises and grows. It makes itself look bigger than it really is. It’s all about feeling too important.

Like the Yetzer Hara! Which means that Hashem is warning us to stay away.

Yeah, because the Yetzer Hara tries to be all chutzpedik and tell us not to listen to Hashem. He says we should do what we want—like lie in bed instead of getting up and saying Modeh Ani.
